# tack

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
The global instructions every Claude Code and Codex session loads, the skills and tools
those sessions call, and each harness's settings and hooks. Per-project profiles here
carry what differs between personal, work, and external checkouts.
<!-- ops:identity end -->

This is one person's working configuration for coding agents, published as a reference
rather than as a package. It is wired to its owner's other projects and hosts, so a
clone does not run as-is. It is more useful to read than to install: the instruction
file, the skills, and the hooks and tests that keep them honest.

## Setup

Once per clone:

    just setup

It points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`, registers the `harness-state` clean filter,
and creates `local/codex/rules/`. `local/` is untracked (see Layout). The work configs
under it come from another host's `local/`, never from `just setup`.

The filter keeps `model` and `modelSettings` in `claude/settings*.json` and the
top-level `model` and `model_reasoning_effort` in `codex/config*.toml` out of
the index: `/model` and `/effort` write them into the live files (the homes
symlink here), and they are session state, not configuration. The working tree
keeps the harness's last pick; a checkout of the file drops it, and the harness
runs on its default model until the next pick. Codex's project trust, the
`[projects."<path>"]` tables it adds to `codex/config*.toml`, is host state and stays
out of the index the same way. So any git command that writes a new blob of
`codex/config.toml` over the live file drops the whole list, on every host at once,
since the checkout is shared through Dropbox. `.githooks/codex-trust` puts it back. At
every turn end the Stop hook below saves the live tables into
`local/codex/trust.toml`, never removing one, and inserts the ones the live file lacks
before its first table header. The `post-checkout`, `post-merge` and `post-rewrite`
hooks insert them right after a switch, a checkout of the file, a merge or a rebase,
in the main checkout only. A hook that fails reports on stderr and exits 0, so a
switch that worked does not exit 1; the next turn end retries. Where no hook runs
(`git stash`, `git reset --hard`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert`, `git rebase --abort`,
`git merge --abort`, a merge stopped on a conflict, a rebase that only fast-forwards, a
fresh clone that has a saved copy), the list is back at the next turn end. A Codex session started before
then asks again. While the main checkout is on a branch older than these hooks,
nothing restores the list until the checkout switches back. A table Codex added since
the last turn end is not saved yet. `local/codex/trust.toml` is machine-owned: capture rewrites it whole, so a comment
added by hand is lost. Restoring also takes group and other access off the live
`codex/config.toml`, which a checkout rewrites with the umask's mode. Nothing prunes the
saved copy: to forget a directory, run `.githooks/codex-trust forget <path>`, which
deletes its table from both files.

After the local-layer rollout, other worktrees and branches made before it show
`codex/config*.toml` as modified, because their blobs still carry trust tables, and a
rebase there can stop on them. `git checkout -- codex/config.toml` in a worktree is
safe, since worktree copies are not live. It drops Codex's bookkeeping the
same way: `screen_reader_detection_done` under `[tui]`, the whole
`[tui.model_availability_nux]` table, and `last_updated` / `last_revision` under
each `[marketplaces.*]` table, so a fresh clone probes once and refetches its
marketplaces. Everything else the harness writes — plugin toggles, marketplace
sources, hook trust hashes — is tracked as usual.

One residual: git decides "modified" from the file's size before it runs the
filter, so a switch whose value changes length leaves the file marked `M` in
`git status` (and `git diff-index`) until the next `git add` of it — `git diff`
is content-true. A Stop hook in both harnesses (`.githooks/harness-state-refresh`,
wired in `claude/settings*.json` and `codex/hooks*.json` through the
`~/.local/bin` link in `links.toml`) stages each harness config
whose filtered diff is empty, so the mark clears at the end of the turn that made
it; it skips while another git process holds the index lock. By hand,
`git add -u -- claude codex` does the same while staging only real changes. Do not `git stash` these files to get past it: the stash tree
equals `HEAD`, so `stash pop` brings back the file without its model pick.
Their tests: `uv run --with pytest pytest .githooks`.

The pre-commit hook refuses any staged path under `local/`, which only `git add -f`
can stage. It also refuses a commit whose staged `AGENTS.md` carries a
hand-edited projects block. That block is generated: change the owning project's
`identity.toml` (or its table in `identity-mirror.toml` in ops, until it adopts) and
run `just projects` in ops, which rewrites it here. The hook
finds ops through the tasks registry and fails loudly when ops is not
registered. Its tests: `uv run --with pytest pytest .githooks/test_pre_commit.py`.

The same hook runs `tools/ops-docs check`, vendored from ops: the identity regions at
the top of this file and of `AGENTS.md` are generated from `identity.toml`, and
`just docs` regenerates them.

## Usage

Things you can take from here without the rest:

- `AGENTS.md`: the global instructions. Claude Code reads it as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`,
  and Codex as `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`. The "Projects" block near the end lists the owner's
  own projects, and the rules refer to their tools (`tasks`, `ops-profile`,
  `host-load`), so read them as an example rather than adopting them wholesale.
- `agents/skills/`: skills in the Agent Skills format. `flow` and `session-logs` are
  written here. The superpowers skills link into the `agents/vendor/superpowers`
  submodule (`git submodule update --init`). The addyosmani/agent-skills ones are
  vendored under their MIT license (`agents/skills/references/`). `curate`, `scope`
  and `tasks` link into a sibling checkout of [tasks](https://github.com/khughitt/tasks)
  and dangle without one; `quick-add` links into a private checkout.
- `.githooks/harness-state-clean`: a git clean filter that keeps `/model` and `/effort`
  picks, Codex bookkeeping and Codex project trust out of committed harness configs.
  It is useful on its own for anyone who versions `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`.
- `tools/tack-link` with `links.toml`: declares every link from a harness home into a
  checkout. It reports drift and never overwrites a real file.

MIT licensed; see `LICENSE`.

## Layout

- `AGENTS.md`: the global instructions; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`
  link to it. Two regions in it are generated: the identity line at the top
  (`just docs`) and the projects block (`just projects` in ops).
- `agents/skills/`: skills. `agents/bin/`: tools. `agents/profiles/`: per-project
  profiles for personal, work, and external checkouts, resolved by ops
  (`docs/specs/2026-09-19-project-profiles-design.md`).
- `claude/` and `codex/`: per-harness settings and hooks. Each home's settings and hooks
  files are symlinks to them: `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` to the plain files,
  `~/.codex-work` to `codex/hooks.work.json`.
- `local/`: untracked, and carried between hosts by Dropbox, not git. It holds
  `claude/settings.work.json`, `codex/config.work.toml` and `codex/rules/`, the files
  a home links to that the repository must not publish. The `~/.claude-work`,
  `~/.codex-work` and `~/.codex/rules` links point into it
  (`docs/specs/2026-09-28-local-layer-design.md`).
- `docs/`: specs, plans, and notes.
- `tools/ops-docs`: vendored from ops; change it there.

## Consumers

Every Claude Code and Codex session on a host whose harness homes link here. ops renders
the projects block into `AGENTS.md` and reads `agents/profiles/` through `ops-profile`.

## Home links

Every link from a harness home into this checkout is listed in `links.toml`:
`[required]` links go on every host; each `[harness.<name>]` group applies only where
that harness's home is a real directory, and only then are its targets checked. A
missing target under `local/` names the remedy: copy it from another host's `local/`,
or run `just setup`. `just link` reports what would change,
`just link --apply` converges this host, and `just link-check` exits non-zero on drift.
Run `just link --apply` once on each host after pulling a change to `links.toml`, and on
a new host after installing a harness. It never overwrites a real file (`refuse`) and
refuses to run from a worktree.

## Renamed from ai

This project was `ai` until 2026-09. Old `ai-<hex>` task ids resolve through the tasks
alias. On a host that synced the rename, run once in this checkout, with no harness
session open: `tasks rename ai tack --adopt`, `just link --apply`, and
`work-link --ensure .worktrees` after moving `.dropbox-work/ai` to `.dropbox-work/tack`.
Until then that host's harness sessions start without instructions, skills or hooks.

## Local layer (2026-09)

The work configs and Codex's rules moved from the tracked tree to `local/`. On a
host that shares this checkout, once Dropbox has synced `local/` there, run
`just link --apply` once, with no Codex or work-home session open.
